tiers.basis: The identity of the maintainer appears in no threshold and under no function the buyer relies on; the buyer is acquiring the code, not the person. Rated on the scale alone.
That releases are published on GitHub changes nothing about what the buyer is paying for or the terms; the buyer's stated end-the-deal conditions do not reach it. Rated on the scale alone.

The buyer's price and its decision to close rest on clean ownership under the MIT licence, and the licence document is the fact the buyer relies on; if the claim were false the deal would not proceed. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a licence or ownership problem with the code".

Shortening is the core of what the buyer is buying; if the product were not a working self-hosted shortener, there is nothing for the buyer's staff to patch and no bargain left. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a small, private link shortener the buyer can run for its customers".

The footprint threshold reaches this claim, but a single image-size figure, even if worse than stated, is too small on its own for the buyer to go back to the seller over; a reader choosing between image variants and sizing storage would act on the figure. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "footprint or resource figures materially worse than stated".

The footprint threshold reaches this claim, but one compressed image figure alone is too small to reopen the price over; a reader choosing the alpine variant would act on the figure when picking hardware and storage. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "footprint or resource figures materially worse than stated".

The resource-figure threshold reaches this claim, but one RAM figure, even if false, is too small alone to send the buyer back to the seller over; a reader planning the instance's hosting would act on it. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "footprint or resource figures materially worse than stated".

The buyer acquires source code it can run and, if need be, maintain itself; no threshold names the project's being finished or alive, and the claim is the maintainer's characterisation rather than a commitment the buyer's plan depends on. Rated on the scale alone.
A decision not to add features costs the buyer nothing; the buyer is buying the tool as described, and no threshold or plan item reaches a refusal of new features. Rated on the scale alone.

The upkeep commitments sit under an item the buyer's plan only uses, on the practice's inference, and no stated threshold names bug fixing; if the promise were not kept, staff would carry fixes in a small codebase, which is costly but does not reopen the price or the terms on its own. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

Security upkeep sits under an item the buyer's plan only uses, on the practice's inference, and no stated threshold names it; if the promise were not kept, staff would track and apply vulnerability fixes themselves, a running cost that does not by itself change the price or the terms. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

The implementation language reaches no threshold and no item the buyer depends on; it bears only on how easily staff could patch, which the reliance statement treats as the practice's inference. Rated on the scale alone.

The hit count is the one piece of visitor data the buyer's price assumes it gets, the outer edge of what recording it will accept; if the software included no hit counting, that condition is breached and the buyer could not restore it by configuration. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "any way visitors are logged or tracked beyond the hit count".
The seller's demo instance sits under an item the buyer's plan does not use at all; the buyer is acquiring the code and would never touch the hosted demo. Rated on the scale alone.

The shortening path is the core of the service the buyer is buying; if it did not exist as described, the one thing the purchase is for fails and nothing the buyer's staff could do in configuration restores it. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a small, private link shortener the buyer can run for its customers".

If false, shortening still works for ordinary URLs and the buyer loses only the absence of a length cap, a restriction its staff would rarely meet in normal link-shortening use. No stated threshold or reliance item names URL length, and the failure would not defeat the core shortening the buyer depends on. Rated on the scale alone.

If expiry logic were absent, the buyer's staff could remove stale links by hand, which the reliance statement treats as a cheap substitution while the service is small. The expiry item is one the buyer uses, not one it depends on. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

If the expiry time could not be chosen per link, links would die or persist on a fixed schedule, and staff could manage the difference manually at small cost. This falls under an item the buyer uses, not one it depends on, and no stated threshold names expiry. Rated on the practice's reading of the buyer's plan.

Custom aliases are named in the item the buyer depends on — shortening with a generated slug or a customer-chosen custom alias — and the buyer is offering the service to its own customers, for whom chosen addresses are a visible part of the product. If the claim were false, the buyer would go back over a missing feature of the core service it is paying for. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a small, private link shortener the buyer can run for its customers".

The redirect path is the other half of the service's core, and its failure would leave every link the buyer's customers share failing or misleading, with no repair in the buyer's staff's power. This defeats an item the buyer depends on outright. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a small, private link shortener the buyer can run for its customers".

The reliance statement's depends item covers redirecting the visitor straight to the destination; an intermediate redirection page would defeat that and degrade or mislead every shared link. If the claim were false the buyer would go back over the behaviour of the service's core path. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "a small, private link shortener the buyer can run for its customers".

If the claim were false the buyer would go back to the seller over this figure alone. Rated against the buyer's stated threshold: "footprint or resource figures materially worse than stated".
